_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Switzerland covering Helvetii (Celtic), Roman conquest, Old Swiss Confederacy (1291 founding oath), expansion, Reformation (Zwingli/Calvin), Thirty Years War neutrality, French Revolutionary Wars, Act of Mediation 1803, Congress of Vienna 1815 (perpetual neutrality recognized), Sonderbund War 1847 (last armed conflict), Federal Constitution 1848, Red Cross founded 1863, League of Nations HQ Geneva, WWII neutrality (controversial), UN membership 2002, direct democracy.

country_profile.government_type: Federal semi-direct democracy under multi-party directorial republic

religion.note: Confessional divide historically central (Reformation, Zwingli Zürich/Calvin Geneva, Catholic cantons vs Reformed, Sonderbund War 1847 last armed conflict); Catholic majority until 1970s; rapid secularization; Islam (Turkish/Balkan immigration); 2009 minaret ban referendum (controversial, 57.5% yes, criticized internationally)

ethnic_groups.name: Swiss German
ethnic_groups.notes: German-speaking; Swiss German (Schwiizerdüütsch) spoken dialect (unintelligible to Standard German speakers); Protestant/Catholic mix; Zürich financial center; Basel pharmaceutical; punctuality stereotype

ethnic_groups.name: Swiss French
ethnic_groups.notes: Romandie (Geneva, Lausanne, Neuchâtel, Jura); speak standard French (not patois); Catholic majority; La Suisse romande; closer to French culture but fiercely Swiss

ethnic_groups.name: Swiss Italian
ethnic_groups.notes: Ticino canton; Italian spoken; southernmost; Mediterranean culture; banking (Lugano); different from northern Switzerland; Ticinese identity

ethnic_groups.name: Romansh
ethnic_groups.notes: ~40k; Graubünden canton; Rhaeto-Romance language (Latin-derived, 5 dialects, Rumantsch Grischun standardized); national language since 1938 (4th official); endangered (UNESCO); symbolic importance; Alpine valleys

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Foreign residents ~25% (among highest in Europe, but citizenship difficult, residence ≠ citizenship): German citizens (~310k), Italian (~320k), Portuguese (~270k, 1980s-90s labor), French (~145k), Kosovar (~110k), Turkish (~80k), Serbian (~90k), British (~50k); no jus soli (birthright citizenship almost impossible, multi-generational foreigners); naturalization difficult (10+ years, local vote, expensive, integration requirements, 2017 eased slightly)

independence.from: Holy Roman Empire (founding oath, Federal Charter, William Tell legend); perpetual neutrality recognized 1815 Congress of Vienna

country_profile.notes_unique: Direct democracy (Bundesversammlung/Federal Assembly weak, referendums/initiatives constant, citizens vote on everything, 4 per year average, world's most direct democracy, 1848 Constitution); Federal Council (Bundesrat, 7 members, collective head of state, rotates presidency annually, 'magic formula' party representation); Perpetual neutrality (since 1815 Congress of Vienna, not invaded WWI/WWII, hosted peace talks, Red Cross); Banking secrecy (1934 law, anonymous accounts, tax haven, Nazi gold WWII controversial, pressure 2000s+, FATCA 2014 US deal, automatic exchange 2018, secrecy eroded but wealth management continues); Red Cross/ICRC (founded 1863 Henry Dunant, Geneva Conventions, neutral humanitarian); Geneva (UN European HQ, WHO, WTO, ICRC, diplomacy center, 'Peace Capital'); CERN (particle physics, Large Hadron Collider, Tim Berners-Lee invented WWW 1989); Watches (luxury, precision, Rolex/Patek Philippe/Omega); Chocolate (Nestlé/Lindt/Toblerone); Cheese (750+ varieties, fondue, raclette); Alps (60% mountainous, Matterhorn, skiing, tourism); Schengen (member) but not EU (referendums rejected 1992/2001, immigration quotas debate, bilateral agreements); Multilingual (4 national languages); Cantons (26, federal system, strong local autonomy); Military service (conscription for men, militia army, fallout shelters for 100% population); Universal healthcare (mandatory private insurance); Women's suffrage 1971 (last in Europe except Liechtenstein, Appenzell Innerrhoden canton held out until 1990 forced by court)

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Karin Keller-Sutter
current_leader.title: President of the Swiss Confederation
current_leader.notes: FDP (Liberal); Finance Minister; rotates annually (ceremonial, 'first among equals'); one of seven Federal Council members; center-right; EU negotiations

head_of_state.name: Federal Council (collective)
head_of_state.title: Bundesrat (7 members)
head_of_state.notes: Unique collective executive; 7 members from 4 main parties (magic formula: SVP 2, SP 2, FDP 2, Mitte 1); rotates presidency annually (2025: Keller-Sutter); consensus government; each heads department; elected by Federal Assembly (not popular vote); stability over personality; no single head

former_leaders.name: Alain Berset
former_leaders.notes: SP (Social Democrats); Health Minister (COVID response, vaccine mandates controversial); President 2018/2023 (twice); charismatic by Swiss standards; retired 2023; longest in council of current era

former_leaders.name: Micheline Calmy-Rey
former_leaders.notes: SP; Foreign Minister; first female President 2007; diplomatic initiatives (Iran talks, Palestine)

former_leaders.name: Ruth Dreifuss
former_leaders.notes: SP; first female Federal Councillor; first Jewish member; Interior Minister (healthcare reform); progressive icon

former_leaders.name: Elisabeth Kopp
former_leaders.notes: FDP; first woman elected to Federal Council; resigned 1989 (scandal, leaked info to husband); breaking glass ceiling

former_leaders.name: System note
former_leaders.notes: Switzerland's Federal Council system (collegiality, no prime minister, rotating presidency) makes individual leaders less prominent. Notable eras: WWII neutrality (Marcel Pilet-Golaz, criticized for Nazi appeasement); Banking secrecy battles 2000s-10s (Hans-Rudolf Merz); Christoph Blocher (SVP, 2004-07, anti-EU hardliner, only Federal Councillor not re-elected, polarizing)

910.name: Helvetii Celts & Roman Helvetia
910.description: The Helvetii, a Celtic people, gave Switzerland its Latin name (Confoederatio Helvetica). Their attempted migration was blocked by Caesar at Bibracte (58 BCE), and the region was integrated into the Roman Empire as part of several provinces.

sub_clusters.name: Helvetii & La Tène Culture
sub_clusters.description: The Helvetii and their La Tène material culture centred on the Swiss Plateau, oppida settlements, and the decision to migrate westward that brought them into conflict with Rome.
key_events: Caesar defeats the Helvetii at the Battle of Bibracte (58 BCE)

930.name: Perpetual Neutrality & Peace of Westphalia
930.description: While the Thirty Years' War devastated surrounding lands, Switzerland maintained its neutrality. The Peace of Westphalia (1648) formally recognised Swiss independence from the Holy Roman Empire and established the principle of perpetual neutrality.

sub_clusters.name: Thirty Years' War & Swiss Neutrality

940.name: Napoleonic Helvetic Republic
940.description: Napoleon's invasion ended the Old Confederacy and imposed the centralised Helvetic Republic (1798–1803), followed by the Act of Mediation restoring cantonal sovereignty. The Congress of Vienna (1815) guaranteed Swiss neutrality in perpetuity.

sub_clusters.name: Helvetic Republic & Act of Mediation
sub_clusters.description: French invasion, the short-lived centralised Helvetic Republic, internal resistance, and Napoleon's Act of Mediation (1803) restoring the confederal structure with six new cantons.
